# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_007_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 3

**1** The tower was being built by six young men who had come with her. Many thousands of other men were bringing stones — some from the deep sea, others from the dry land — and handing them to the six, who received them and built with them. **2** All the stones dragged from the deep sea were placed into the building just as they were, for they were smooth and fit precisely at the joints. They locked together so tightly that their seams could not be detected; the whole tower appeared as though it had been built from a single stone. **3** As for the stones brought from the dry land — some of these they discarded, others they placed into the building, and others they broke apart and threw far from the tower. **4** Many other stones were lying around the tower unused — some thrown far away, some cracked, some white and round and unable to fit into the building. **5** I saw other stones being flung far away: some landed on the road but did not stay there, rolling off into trackless ground; others fell into fire and burned; others landed near the water but could not roll in, though they seemed to strain toward it. **6** When she had shown me these things she made to leave. I said, "Lady, what use is it to me to see all this if I do not know what it means?" She turned to me and said, "You are a bold one, wanting to know all about the tower." "Even so, please tell me, lady." **7** "This tower," she said, "is the Church." "And who are the six young men building it?" "They are the holy angels of God who were created first of all, to whom the Lord entrusted all his creation — to build it up, increase it, and govern it. Through them the building of the tower will be completed." **8** "And the thousands of others bringing stones — who are they?" "These also are holy angels of God, but the six are over them. The tower will be completed, and all will rejoice together around it and give glory to God, because the building has been finished." **9** "Lady, I would like to understand what the stones mean," I said. She replied, "The bright, square stones that fit together at their joints — these are the apostles and bishops and teachers and deacons who walked in the holiness of God and served him purely and reverently in their various offices. Some of these have already fallen asleep; others are still living. They were always in agreement with one another, and they lived at peace with one another. **10** That is why their joints fit together so precisely in the tower." "And those dragged from the deep sea?" "These are those who have suffered for the name of the Lord." **11** "And those from dry land?" "Those who did not suffer, but whose holy way of life pleased God as they walked in his commandments." "And those who are rejected — who are they?" **12** "Those who have sinned and wish to repent. That is why they have not been thrown far from the tower — they can still be used in the building if they repent. But they must repent now, while the tower is still being built. Once the tower is finished there will be no more room for repentance — such persons will be cast aside." **13** "And the rejected, cracked ones?" "These are the sons of wickedness who have believed hypocritically and in whom no wickedness has ceased. They have no salvation, for they are unfit for the building on account of their wickedness." **14** "And the white round ones that will not fit?" "How long will you be slow to understand?" she said. "These are those who have faith but also possess the wealth of this age. When tribulation comes, they deny their Lord on account of their riches and their business dealings." "When will they be useful for the building?" "When their wealth is stripped away — the wealth that has bewitched them — then they will be useful to God. For just as a round stone cannot become square unless it is cut and something is taken from it, so those who are wealthy in this age cannot be useful to the Lord unless their wealth is cut away from them. **15** Learn this first from your own life: when you were wealthy you were useless, but now you are useful and profitable for life. Be useful to God, for you yourself were cut from this very stone."

---

### Council Notes

This is the theological center of the Vision section. The tower allegory is a masterwork of early Christian typology:

- **Stones from the sea** = martyrs (drawn from the depth of suffering)
- **Stones from dry land** = those who kept commandments without martyrdom
- **Rejected stones** = sinners who still have opportunity to repent (critical for the Shepherd's doctrine)
- **Cracked stones** = hypocrites who never truly changed
- **Round white stones** = the wealthy — their wealth prevents them from fitting the Church's shape

The note in v. 15 that Hermas himself was once such a round stone is a rare autobiographical moment connecting the visionary to his own allegory.

The stones straining toward the water (v. 5) likely represent those who desire baptism (or re-baptism) but cannot obtain it — a poignant early Christian image.
